requirements.quote: Complex fields are named and then followed by a list of fields surrounded by a pair of matching braces.
requirements.condition: When representing a complex field using the document's custom packet or frame format.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the complex field's name before its field list and surround the list with matching braces.
requirements.why_checkable: A parsed diagram can be checked for the required name-before-list structure and matching braces.

requirements.quote: Each field in this list is separated by commas.
requirements.condition: When a complex-field list contains individual fields.
requirements.required_behavior: Separate the individual fields with commas.
requirements.why_checkable: The separators between fields in a diagram can be inspected mechanically.

requirements.quote: Individual fields include length information, plus indications about fixed value, optionality, or repetitions.
requirements.condition: When an individual field has a fixed value, is optional, or is repeated in the custom format.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent its length and the applicable fixed-value, optionality, or repetition indication.
requirements.why_checkable: Each field declaration can be parsed to verify that length and applicable property markers are present.

requirements.quote: Individual fields use the following notational conventions, with all lengths in bits:
requirements.condition: When interpreting or producing a length in an individual-field declaration.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret and express the declared length in bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Declared lengths can be evaluated consistently as bit counts.

requirements.quote: x (A): Indicates that x is A bits long
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (A)".
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or parse x as exactly A bits long.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept x with a length different from A bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The actual field width can be compared directly with the declared constant A.

requirements.quote: x (i): Indicates that x holds an integer value using the variable- length encoding described in Section 16
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (i)".
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or parse x as an integer using the variable-length encoding described in Section 16.
requirements.why_checkable: The required encoding is identified, but its definition is outside this chunk, so this chunk alone does not provide complete evidence for a concrete encoding check.

requirements.quote: x (A..B): Indicates that x can be any length from A to B;
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (A..B)" with both bounds present.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or accept x only when its length is between A and B, inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept x with a length below A or above B.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's measured bit length can be compared with the declared lower and upper bounds.

requirements.quote: A can be omitted to indicate a minimum of zero bits, and B can be omitted to indicate no set upper limit;
requirements.condition: When A is omitted from a field-length range.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the minimum permitted length as zero bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not infer a positive minimum length solely from the omitted A bound.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser or encoder's effective lower bound for an omitted A can be verified as zero.

requirements.quote: A can be omitted to indicate a minimum of zero bits, and B can be omitted to indicate no set upper limit;
requirements.condition: When B is omitted from a field-length range.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the field as having no set upper length limit from this notation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not infer a finite upper bound solely from the omitted B bound.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser or encoder can be tested to ensure the notation itself does not impose a finite upper bound.

requirements.quote: values in this format always end on a byte boundary
requirements.condition: When a field uses the "x (A..B)" length-range format, including an omitted bound.
requirements.required_behavior: End the field value on a byte boundary.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept such a field value ending between byte boundaries.
requirements.why_checkable: The ending bit offset can be checked for divisibility by eight.

requirements.quote: x (L) = C: Indicates that x has a fixed value of C;
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (L) = C".
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or accept x with the value C.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept a value for x other than C.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded field value can be compared directly with the declared constant C.

requirements.quote: the length of x is described by L, which can use any of the length forms above
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (L) = C".
requirements.required_behavior: Determine and enforce x's length according to the length form used for L.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected L form supplies a concrete fixed, variable-integer, or ranged length rule that can be applied to x.

requirements.quote: x (L) = C..D: Indicates that x has a value in the range from C to D, inclusive, with the length described by L, as above
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (L) = C..D".
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or accept x only with a value from C through D, including both endpoints.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept a value below C or above D.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded value can be compared directly with the inclusive numeric bounds.

requirements.quote: x (L) = C..D: Indicates that x has a value in the range from C to D, inclusive, with the length described by L, as above
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (L) = C..D".
requirements.required_behavior: Determine and enforce x's length according to the length form used for L.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected L form supplies a concrete length rule that can be checked independently of the value range.

requirements.quote: [x (L)]: Indicates that x is optional and has a length of L
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "[x (L)]".
requirements.required_behavior: Permit x to be absent; when x is present, encode or parse it with length L.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require x to be present.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can cover both absence and presence, and can verify the declared length in the presence case.

requirements.quote: x (L) ...: Indicates that x is repeated zero or more times and that each instance has a length of L
requirements.condition: When a field is declared using the form "x (L) ...".
requirements.required_behavior: Permit zero or more instances of x and encode or parse every instance with length L.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require at least one instance, and do not use a length other than L for any instance.
requirements.why_checkable: Instance count can be tested at zero and above, and every instance width can be compared with L.

requirements.quote: This document uses network byte order (that is, big endian) values.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a multi-byte value defined by this document.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use little-endian or another byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: Known multi-byte values can be encoded and decoded to verify most-significant-byte-first ordering.

requirements.quote: Fields are placed starting from the high-order bits of each byte.
requirements.condition: When placing fields within a byte.
requirements.required_behavior: Place fields beginning at the byte's high-order bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not begin field placement at the byte's low-order bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit offsets of fields within encoded bytes can be inspected directly.
